source.text: וַיֶּאֶסֹ֧ף יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶת־כָּל־שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁכֶ֑מָה וַיִּקְרָא֩ לְזִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּלְרָאשָׁ֗יו וּלְשֹֽׁפְטָיו֙ וּלְשֹׁ֣טְרָ֔יו וַיִּֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered Joshua all [the] tribes of Israel to Shechem, and summoned [the] elders of Israel and its heads and its judges and its officers, and they presented themselves before the God.

en.L: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and he summoned the elders of Israel and its heads and its judges and its officers, and they presented themselves before God.
en.B: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He called for the elders of Israel, its leaders, its judges and its officers, and they took their stand before God.
en.R: Joshua brought all the tribes of Israel together at Shechem. He called for Israel's elders, leaders, judges and officers, and they came and stood in front of God.

sw.L: Na Yoshua akakusanya makabila yote ya Israeli huko Shekemu, akawaita wazee wa Israeli na wakuu wake na waamuzi wake na maafisa wake, nao wakajihudhurisha mbele za Mungu.
sw.B: Yoshua aliyakusanya makabila yote ya Israeli huko Shekemu. Akawaita wazee wa Israeli, viongozi wake, waamuzi wake na maafisa wake, nao wakasimama mbele za Mungu.
sw.R: Yoshua aliyakusanya pamoja makabila yote ya Israeli huko Shekemu. Akawaita wazee, viongozi, waamuzi na maafisa wa Israeli, nao wakaja wakasimama mbele za Mungu.

es.L: Y Josué reunió a todas las tribus de Israel en Siquem, y convocó a los ancianos de Israel, y a sus cabezas, y a sus jueces, y a sus oficiales, y se presentaron delante de Dios.
es.B: Josué reunió en Siquem a todas las tribus de Israel. Llamó a los ancianos de Israel, a sus jefes, a sus jueces y a sus oficiales, y ellos se presentaron delante de Dios.
es.R: Josué reunió en Siquem a todas las tribus de Israel. Llamó a los ancianos, jefes, jueces y oficiales de Israel, y ellos vinieron y se pusieron delante de Dios.

decisions.choice: Shechem: the town in the hill country between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, a place full of Israel's early memories
decisions.reason: Shechem is where God first promised the land to Abraham and where Abraham built his first altar in it (Genesis 12:6-7). Jacob bought land there (Genesis 33:18-20), and there he had his household put away their foreign gods and buried them under the oak (Genesis 35:2-4). Joshua had read the law to all Israel between the two mountains beside it (8:30-35). Joshua's call to put away foreign gods (verses 14, 23) is made in the same place.

decisions.choice: presented themselves before God: took their places formally in God's presence
decisions.reason: The verb means to take one's stand, to present oneself before a superior (Exodus 19:17; 1 Samuel 10:19). "Before God" marks the gathering as an act of worship at a holy place: verse 26 speaks of the sanctuary of the LORD at Shechem.

decisions.choice: elders, heads, judges and officers: Israel's leaders, the same four groups as in 23:2
decisions.reason: Elders were the senior men of the clans and towns. "Heads" are the chiefs of tribes and families. Judges settled disputes (Deuteronomy 16:18). The officers helped organize the people and passed on orders (1:10; 3:2). Joshua had already called these leaders together once (23:2); this second gathering includes all the tribes.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "heads", meaning chiefs. Balanced and Readable say "leaders" so the word is not read as body parts.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֗ר יָשְׁב֤וּ אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ מֵֽעוֹלָ֔ם תֶּ֛רַח אֲבִ֥י אַבְרָהָ֖ם וַאֲבִ֣י נָח֑וֹר וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joshua to all the people, thus says Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, beyond the River lived your fathers from long ago, Terah, [the] father of Abraham and [the] father of Nahor, and they served gods other.

en.L: And Joshua said to all the people, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: 'Beyond the River your fathers lived from long ago, Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor, and they served other gods.
en.B: Then Joshua told all the people, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: 'In ancient times your ancestors lived on the far side of the River, Terah, father of Abraham and of Nahor, and they served other gods.
en.R: Joshua said to all the people, "Here is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: 'Long, long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River. Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor, was one of them. They served other gods.

sw.L: Na Yoshua akawaambia watu wote, "Hivi ndivyo asemavyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli: 'Ng'ambo ya Mto baba zenu waliishi tangu zamani, Tera baba wa Abrahamu na baba wa Nahori, nao walitumikia miungu mingine.
sw.B: Ndipo Yoshua akawaambia watu wote, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, anasema hivi: 'Zamani za kale baba zenu waliishi upande wa pili wa Mto, yaani Tera, baba wa Abrahamu na wa Nahori, nao walitumikia miungu mingine.
sw.R: Yoshua aliwaambia watu wote, "Hiki ndicho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, anachosema: 'Zamani sana babu zenu waliishi upande wa pili wa Mto Frati. Tera, baba wa Abrahamu na Nahori, alikuwa mmoja wao. Walitumikia miungu mingine.

es.L: Y dijo Josué a todo el pueblo: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: “Al otro lado del Río habitaron {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}} desde la antigüedad, Taré, padre de Abraham y padre de Nacor, y sirvieron a otros dioses.
es.B: Entonces Josué dijo a todo el pueblo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: “En tiempos antiguos {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} vivían al otro lado del Río, Taré, padre de Abraham y de Nacor, y servían a otros dioses.
es.R: Josué le dijo a todo el pueblo: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: “Hace muchísimo tiempo, {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} vivían al otro lado del río Éufrates. Uno de ellos era Taré, el padre de Abraham y de Nacor. Ellos servían a otros dioses.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD: Joshua speaks God's words as a messenger, and God speaks as "I" through verse 13
decisions.reason: This is the form a prophet uses to pass on a message word for word (Exodus 4:22; 5:1). From here to the end of verse 13 God himself tells Israel's story in the first person: "I took", "I gave", "I sent". In verse 14 Joshua goes on in his own voice.

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates; Terah's family lived beyond it, in Ur and Haran
decisions.reason: "The River" with no name means the Euphrates (1:4; Genesis 31:21). Terah, his sons Abraham and Nahor, and their family lived in Ur and then Haran, both beyond the Euphrates as seen from Canaan (Genesis 11:27-32).

decisions.choice: they served other gods: Israel's ancestors worshiped other gods before God called Abraham
decisions.reason: Israel's story does not begin with a faithful family but with people who served other gods. God's choice of Abraham was his own act of grace, not a reward. The verb "serve" runs through the whole chapter, and Joshua comes back to these same gods "beyond the River" in verses 14-15.

decisions.choice: from long ago: in ancient times
decisions.reason: The phrase means "from of old", from the distant past, not "forever".

decisions.choice: the Euphrates River; was one of them
decisions.reason: Readable names the river, following meaning decision m2, and makes Terah a sentence of his own, as one of those ancestors.

decisions.choice: double quotes for Joshua, single quotes for God's words
decisions.reason: Joshua's speech opens here and runs to the end of verse 15. The words of God he passes on are set inside it in single quotes, which open here and close at the end of verse 13.

decisions.choice: "Mto Frati" (the Euphrates)
decisions.reason: "The River" without a name means the Euphrates. Literal and Balanced keep "Mto"; Readable names it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "el Río" (L, B); "el río Éufrates" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says simply "the River", the great river Euphrates. Literal and Balanced keep the name with a capital, as the English does; Readable names it. The LORD's words stand inside Joshua's, so they take the inner Spanish quotation marks “ ” through verse 13.

decisions.choice: plural forms through Joshua's speech and the LORD's words in it ("sus padres", "los saqué" by default; "vuestros padres", "os saqué" with the plural-you setting)
decisions.reason: The whole people is addressed, and the Hebrew is plural, so every second-person form takes the plural-you setting, as in chapter 23.

source.text: וָ֠אֶקַּח אֶת־אֲבִיכֶ֤ם אֶת־אַבְרָהָם֙ מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֔ר וָאוֹלֵ֥ךְ אוֹת֖וֹ בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וָאַרְבֶּה֙ אֶת־זַרְע֔וֹ וָֽאֶתֶּן־ל֖וֹ אֶת־יִצְחָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And I took your father Abraham from beyond the River, and I led him through all [the] land of Canaan, and I multiplied his offspring, and I gave to him Isaac.

en.L: And I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan, and I multiplied his offspring, and I gave him Isaac.
en.B: But I took your father Abraham from the far side of the River and led him all through the land of Canaan. I made his descendants many, and I gave him Isaac.
en.R: But I took your ancestor Abraham from there, on the other side of the River. I led him all through the land of Canaan, and I gave him many descendants. I gave him a son, Isaac.

sw.L: Nami nikamchukua baba yenu Abrahamu kutoka ng'ambo ya Mto, nikamwongoza katika nchi yote ya Kanaani, nikauzidisha uzao wake, nikampa Isaka.
sw.B: Lakini nilimchukua baba yenu Abrahamu kutoka upande wa pili wa Mto, nikamwongoza katika nchi yote ya Kanaani. Nikawafanya wazao wake kuwa wengi, nikampa Isaka.
sw.R: Lakini nilimchukua babu yenu Abrahamu kutoka huko, upande wa pili wa Mto. Nilimwongoza katika nchi yote ya Kanaani, nikampa wazao wengi. Nilimpa mwana, Isaka.

es.L: Y yo tomé a {{plural_you:su padre|vuestro padre}} Abraham del otro lado del Río, y lo conduje por toda la tierra de Canaán, y multipliqué su descendencia, y le di a Isaac.
es.B: Pero yo tomé a {{plural_you:su padre|vuestro padre}} Abraham del otro lado del Río y lo guie por toda la tierra de Canaán. Multipliqué su descendencia y le di a Isaac.
es.R: Pero yo saqué de allí, del otro lado del río, a {{plural_you:su antepasado|vuestro antepasado}} Abraham. Lo guie por toda la tierra de Canaán y le di muchos descendientes. Le di un hijo, Isaac.

decisions.choice: I took ... and led him: God's call of Abraham and his travels through Canaan
decisions.reason: God called Abraham to leave his country and go to the land he would show him (Genesis 12:1-6), and told him to walk through its length and breadth (Genesis 13:17). The verbs put God, not Abraham, at the center: God took him and God led him.

decisions.choice: and I took: God's act set against the ancestors' worship of other gods
decisions.reason: The plain "and" follows the story on, but after verse 2 it also marks a contrast: the family served other gods, and God took Abraham out of it.

decisions.choice: and I multiplied, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) give a shorter spelling of the verb; the reading the scribes marked (qere) gives the full form. Both mean "and I multiplied".

decisions.choice: I multiplied his offspring and gave him Isaac: the promise of many descendants, and the son born to Sarah
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham descendants as many as the stars (Genesis 15:5), and the promised son Isaac was born in his old age (Genesis 21:1-3).

decisions.choice: But; ancestor (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "But" to bring out the contrast of meaning decision m2. Readable says "ancestor" for "father", since Abraham lived long before the people listening.

source.text: וָאֶתֵּ֣ן לְיִצְחָ֔ק אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְאֶת־עֵשָׂ֑ו וָאֶתֵּ֨ן לְעֵשָׂ֜ו אֶת־הַ֤ר שֵׂעִיר֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אוֹת֔וֹ וְיַעֲקֹ֥ב וּבָנָ֖יו יָרְד֥וּ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I gave to Isaac Jacob and Esau, and I gave to Esau [the] hill country of Seir to possess it, and Jacob and his sons went down [to] Egypt.

en.L: And I gave Isaac Jacob and Esau. And I gave Esau the hill country of Seir to possess it, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
en.B: To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Seir as his own, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
en.R: I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hills of Seir to be his land. But Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.

sw.L: Nami nikampa Isaka Yakobo na Esau. Nikampa Esau nchi ya milima ya Seiri aimiliki, lakini Yakobo na wanawe wakashuka Misri.
sw.B: Isaka nilimpa Yakobo na Esau. Esau nilimpa nchi ya milima ya Seiri iwe yake, lakini Yakobo na wanawe walishuka Misri.
sw.R: Nilimpa Isaka wana wawili, Yakobo na Esau. Nilimpa Esau milima ya Seiri iwe nchi yake. Lakini Yakobo na wanawe walishuka Misri.

es.L: Y a Isaac le di a Jacob y a Esaú. Y a Esaú le di la región montañosa de Seír para que la poseyera, pero Jacob y sus hijos descendieron a Egipto.
es.B: A Isaac le di a Jacob y a Esaú. A Esaú le di la región montañosa de Seír como posesión suya, pero Jacob y sus hijos bajaron a Egipto.
es.R: A Isaac le di dos hijos, Jacob y Esaú. A Esaú le di las montañas de Seír para que fueran su tierra. Pero Jacob y sus hijos bajaron a Egipto.

decisions.choice: the hill country of Seir: the mountains of Edom, south-east of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Esau settled in Seir, and his descendants became the people of Edom (Genesis 36:8). God had given that land to Esau's descendants and told Israel not to take it (Deuteronomy 2:5).

decisions.choice: but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt: a contrast with Esau
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "Jacob" first to set him against Esau. Esau received his land at once; Jacob, the son of the promise, went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:1-7), and his descendants had to wait for theirs.

decisions.choice: two sons; the hills of Seir
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jacob and Esau were Isaac's sons, and calls the hill country "hills".

source.text: וָאֶשְׁלַ֞ח אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ וָאֶגֹּ֣ף אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ וְאַחַ֖ר הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I sent Moses and Aaron, and I plagued Egypt according to what I did in its midst, and afterward I brought out you.

en.L: And I sent Moses and Aaron, and I plagued Egypt by what I did in its midst; and afterward I brought you out.
en.B: I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with plagues by what I did among its people. After that I brought you out.
en.R: Then I sent Moses and Aaron. I struck Egypt with plagues by the things I did there. After that I brought you out.

sw.L: Nami nikawatuma Musa na Haruni, nikaipiga Misri kwa yale niliyoyafanya katikati yake; na baadaye nikawatoa ninyi.
sw.B: Niliwatuma Musa na Haruni, nikaipiga Misri kwa mapigo kwa yale niliyoyafanya kati ya watu wake. Baada ya hayo niliwatoa ninyi.
sw.R: Kisha niliwatuma Musa na Haruni. Niliipiga Misri kwa mapigo kwa mambo niliyofanya huko. Baada ya hayo niliwatoa ninyi.

es.L: Y envié a Moisés y a Aarón, y herí a Egipto con lo que hice en medio de él; y después {{plural_you:los|os}} saqué.
es.B: Envié a Moisés y a Aarón, y castigué a Egipto con plagas por lo que hice entre su gente. Después {{plural_you:los|os}} saqué de allí.
es.R: Después envié a Moisés y a Aarón. Castigué a Egipto con plagas por las cosas que hice allí. Después {{plural_you:los|os}} saqué.

decisions.choice: plagued: struck with blows of disaster
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or deal a blow, often with disease or disaster. Here it sums up the plagues God sent on Egypt (Exodus 7-12).

decisions.choice: by what I did in its midst: the signs God worked inside Egypt
decisions.reason: The phrase explains how God struck Egypt: by the wonders he did among its people (Exodus 3:20).

decisions.choice: I brought you out: the people listening are addressed as those who came out
decisions.reason: Most of those who came out of Egypt had died in the wilderness (5:4-6). God speaks to the people as one people through the generations, so their parents' rescue is theirs too. Verses 6-7 move between "your fathers" and "you" in the same way.

decisions.choice: struck ... with plagues
decisions.reason: One Hebrew verb means "strike with plagues". Balanced and Readable use two words to say so.

source.text: וָֽאוֹצִ֤יא אֶת־אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וַתָּבֹ֖אוּ הַיָּ֑מָּה וַיִּרְדְּפ֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם אַחֲרֵ֧י אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֛ם בְּרֶ֥כֶב וּבְפָרָשִׁ֖ים יַם־סֽוּף׃

records.literal_gloss: And I brought out your fathers from Egypt, and you came to the sea; and pursued Egypt after your fathers with chariots and with horsemen [to the] Sea of Reeds.

en.L: And I brought your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea; and Egypt pursued your fathers with chariots and with horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.
en.B: When I brought your ancestors out of Egypt and you reached the sea, the Egyptians chased after your ancestors with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea.
en.R: I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptian army chased them with chariots and men on horses all the way to the Red Sea.

sw.L: Nami nikawatoa baba zenu kutoka Misri, nanyi mkafika baharini; na Wamisri wakawafuatia baba zenu kwa magari na wapanda farasi hadi Bahari ya Matete.
sw.B: Nilipowatoa baba zenu kutoka Misri nanyi mkafika baharini, Wamisri waliwafuatia baba zenu kwa magari ya vita na wapanda farasi hadi Bahari ya Shamu.
sw.R: Niliwatoa babu zenu kutoka Misri, nanyi mkafika baharini. Jeshi la Misri liliwafuatia kwa magari ya vita na watu waliopanda farasi mpaka Bahari ya Shamu.

es.L: Y saqué a {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}} de Egipto, y {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} al mar; y Egipto persiguió a {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}} con carros y jinetes hasta el mar de los Juncos.
es.B: Cuando saqué de Egipto a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} y {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} al mar, los egipcios persiguieron a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} con carros y jinetes hasta el mar Rojo.
es.R: Saqué de Egipto a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}, y {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} al mar. El ejército egipcio los persiguió con carros y hombres a caballo hasta el mar Rojo.

decisions.choice: your fathers ... you: the ancestors and the hearers spoken of as one people
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the speech moves between "your fathers" and "you". The people at Shechem are treated as having been there at the sea.

decisions.choice: Egypt: the Egyptians, that is, their army
decisions.reason: The name of the country stands for its people, and here for the army that rode out after Israel (Exodus 14:9).

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel crossed when leaving Egypt
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name means "Sea of Reeds". It is the sea of Exodus 13:18 and 15:4, which God dried up for Israel (2:10; 4:23).

decisions.choice: the Egyptians / the Egyptian army; the Red Sea
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "Egypt" and "Sea of Reeds". Balanced and Readable say who pursued and use the familiar name of the sea, as in 2:10 and 4:23. Readable says "men on horses" for "horsemen".

decisions.choice: "Bahari ya Matete" (Literal); "Bahari ya Shamu" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus in Swahili: Literal keeps the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds"; the other levels use the familiar name of the sea.

decisions.choice: "el mar de los Juncos" (L); "el mar Rojo" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 13:18: Literal keeps the Hebrew name, "sea of reeds"; Balanced and Readable use the name Spanish readers know.

source.text: וַיִּצְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּ֨שֶׂם מַֽאֲפֵ֜ל בֵּינֵיכֶ֣ם׀וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּצְרִ֗ים וַיָּבֵ֨א עָלָ֤יו אֶת־הַיָּם֙ וַיְכַסֵּ֔הוּ וַתִּרְאֶ֨ינָה֙ עֵינֵיכֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֖יתִי בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וַתֵּשְׁב֥וּ בַמִּדְבָּ֖ר יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they cried out to Yahweh, and he put darkness between you and between the Egyptians, and he brought upon them the sea, and it covered them; and saw your eyes what I did in Egypt; and you lived in the wilderness days many.

en.L: And they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put darkness between you and the Egyptians, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought the sea upon them, and it covered them; and your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. And you lived in the wilderness many days.
en.B: Then they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set darkness between you and the Egyptians. He brought the sea over them, and it covered them. You saw with your own eyes what I did in Egypt. Then you lived in the wilderness for a long time.
en.R: Your ancestors cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put darkness between you and the Egyptians. He made the sea come back over the Egyptians and cover them. You saw with your own eyes what I did to Egypt. Then you lived in the desert for a long time.

sw.L: Nao wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaweka giza kati yenu na Wamisri, akaileta bahari juu yao, ikawafunika; na macho yenu yakaona niliyoyafanya Misri. Nanyi mkaishi nyikani siku nyingi.
sw.B: Ndipo walipomlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaweka giza kati yenu na Wamisri. Akaileta bahari juu yao, ikawafunika. Mliona kwa macho yenu wenyewe niliyoyafanya Misri. Kisha mkaishi nyikani kwa muda mrefu.
sw.R: Babu zenu walimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awasaidie, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaweka giza kati yenu na Wamisri. Akayarudisha maji ya bahari juu ya Wamisri, yakawafunika. Mliona kwa macho yenu wenyewe niliyoifanyia Misri. Kisha mliishi jangwani kwa muda mrefu.

es.L: Y clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso oscuridad entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y los egipcios, y trajo sobre ellos el mar, y los cubrió; y {{plural_you:sus ojos|vuestros ojos}} vieron lo que hice en Egipto. Y {{plural_you:habitaron|habitasteis}} en el desierto muchos días.
es.B: Entonces clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso oscuridad entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y los egipcios. Hizo venir el mar sobre ellos, y los cubrió. {{plural_you:Ustedes vieron|Vosotros visteis}} con {{plural_you:sus propios ojos|vuestros propios ojos}} lo que hice en Egipto. Después {{plural_you:vivieron|vivisteis}} en el desierto mucho tiempo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Sus antepasados|Vuestros antepasados}} clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} pidiendo ayuda, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso oscuridad entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y los egipcios. Hizo que el mar volviera sobre los egipcios y los cubriera. {{plural_you:Ustedes vieron|Vosotros visteis}} con {{plural_you:sus propios ojos|vuestros propios ojos}} lo que hice con Egipto. Después {{plural_you:vivieron|vivisteis}} en el desierto mucho tiempo.

decisions.choice: darkness ... the sea covered them: the night at the sea in Exodus 14
decisions.reason: When the Egyptians drew near, Israel cried out to the LORD (Exodus 14:10). The cloud stood between the two camps, dark on the Egyptians' side (Exodus 14:19-20), and the returning sea covered Pharaoh's army (Exodus 14:27-28).

decisions.choice: they cried out to the LORD, and he put ...: God speaks of himself by name, then again as "I"
decisions.reason: In the middle of God's own words the sentence speaks of "the LORD" and "he", then turns back to "what I did". Such changes of person are common in Hebrew speech and do not mean someone else has begun speaking.

decisions.choice: your eyes saw: you were eyewitnesses
decisions.reason: The phrase stresses that this was seen, not only heard about (Deuteronomy 4:3; 11:7). The oldest of those listening had been children or young men then (Numbers 14:29-31), and the whole people is treated as having been there.

decisions.choice: many days: a long time, the forty years in the wilderness
decisions.reason: "Many days" means a long time. Israel lived in the wilderness forty years (5:6; Numbers 14:33).

decisions.choice: Your ancestors ... for help
decisions.reason: Readable names who cried out, since "they" has no clear subject in English after verse 6, and adds "for help" to show why.

source.text: וָאָבִ֣יא אֶתְכֶ֗ם אֶל־אֶ֤רֶץ הָאֱמֹרִי֙ הַיּוֹשֵׁב֙ בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ אִתְּכֶ֑ם וָאֶתֵּ֨ן אוֹתָ֤ם בְּיֶדְכֶם֙ וַתִּֽירְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־אַרְצָ֔ם וָאַשְׁמִידֵ֖ם מִפְּנֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I brought you to [the] land of the Amorites, the one living on [the] other side of the Jordan, and they fought with you, and I gave them into your hand, and you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them from before you.

en.L: And I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived on the other side of the Jordan, and they fought with you; and I gave them into your hand, and you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them from before you.
en.B: I brought you into the land of the Amorites who lived east of the Jordan. They fought against you, but I handed them over to you. You took their land as your own, and I wiped them out ahead of you.
en.R: Then I brought you to the land of the Amorites, who lived on the east side of the Jordan River. They fought against you, but I let you defeat them. You took over their land, and I destroyed them as you came.

sw.L: Nami nikawaleta katika nchi ya Waamori waliokaa ng'ambo ya Yordani, nao wakapigana nanyi; nami nikawatia mkononi mwenu, nanyi mkaimiliki nchi yao, nami nikawaangamiza mbele yenu.
sw.B: Niliwaleta katika nchi ya Waamori walioishi upande wa mashariki wa Yordani. Walipigana nanyi, lakini niliwatia mikononi mwenu. Mliichukua nchi yao iwe yenu, nami nikawaangamiza mbele yenu.
sw.R: Kisha niliwaleta katika nchi ya Waamori, walioishi upande wa mashariki wa Mto Yordani. Walipigana nanyi, lakini niliwawezesha kuwashinda. Mliichukua nchi yao, nami nikawaangamiza mlipokuwa mkija.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:los|os}} traje a la tierra de los amorreos que habitaban al otro lado del Jordán, y pelearon contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; y los entregué en {{plural_you:su mano|vuestra mano}}, y {{plural_you:tomaron|tomasteis}} posesión de su tierra, y los destruí delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} llevé a la tierra de los amorreos que vivían al este del Jordán. Ellos pelearon contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero yo {{plural_you:se los|os los}} entregué. {{plural_you:Tomaron|Tomasteis}} posesión de su tierra, y yo los exterminé delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Después {{plural_you:los|os}} llevé a la tierra de los amorreos, que vivían al lado este del río Jordán. Ellos pelearon contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} di la victoria. {{plural_you:Se apoderaron|Os apoderasteis}} de su tierra, y yo los destruí a medida que {{plural_you:avanzaban|avanzabais}}.

decisions.choice: the Amorites beyond the Jordan: the kingdoms of Sihon and Og, east of the river
decisions.reason: Seen from Shechem, "the other side of the Jordan" is the east. Israel defeated Sihon and Og, the two Amorite kings there, and took their land (Numbers 21:21-35; Joshua 2:10; 12:1-6).

decisions.choice: I gave them into your hand: I gave you victory over them
decisions.reason: To give someone "into the hand" of another is to put them in that person's power (Deuteronomy 2:24; Joshua 6:2).

decisions.choice: and I brought, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have a longer form of the verb; the reading the scribes marked (qere) has the usual short form. Both mean "and I brought".

decisions.choice: east of the Jordan; handed them over / let you defeat them; wiped them out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the direction, following meaning decision m1, and put "gave them into your hand" in plain words.

source.text: וַיָּ֨קָם בָּלָ֤ק בֶּן־צִפּוֹר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֔ב וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח וַיִּקְרָ֛א לְבִלְעָ֥ם בֶּן־בְּע֖וֹר לְקַלֵּ֥ל אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, and fought against Israel; and he sent and summoned Balaam son of Beor to curse you.

en.L: And Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel; and he sent and summoned Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
en.B: Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up and made war on Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to put a curse on you.
en.R: Balak son of Zippor, the king of Moab, came out to fight Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor and asked him to curse you.

sw.L: Na Balaki mwana wa Sipori, mfalme wa Moabu, akainuka akapigana na Israeli; akatuma akamwita Balaamu mwana wa Beori ili awalaani.
sw.B: Kisha Balaki mwana wa Sipori, mfalme wa Moabu, aliinuka akapigana vita na Israeli. Akatuma watu wamwite Balaamu mwana wa Beori ili awalaani.
sw.R: Balaki mwana wa Sipori, mfalme wa Moabu, alitoka kupigana na Israeli. Alimwita Balaamu mwana wa Beori, akamwomba awalaani.

es.L: Y se levantó Balac hijo de Zipor, rey de Moab, y peleó contra Israel; y envió a llamar a Balaam hijo de Beor para que {{plural_you:los|os}} maldijera.
es.B: Entonces Balac hijo de Zipor, rey de Moab, se levantó e hizo guerra contra Israel. Mandó llamar a Balaam hijo de Beor para que {{plural_you:los|os}} maldijera.
es.R: Balac hijo de Zipor, el rey de Moab, salió a pelear contra Israel. Mandó llamar a Balaam hijo de Beor y le pidió que {{plural_you:los|os}} maldijera.

decisions.choice: Balak and Balaam: the story of Numbers 22-24
decisions.reason: Balak, king of Moab, was afraid of Israel camped on the plains of Moab and hired the seer Balaam from the Euphrates region to curse them (Numbers 22:2-6).

decisions.choice: fought against Israel: set himself against Israel as an enemy
decisions.reason: Numbers tells of no battle between Moab and Israel. Balak's war was by curse: he hoped a curse would let him defeat Israel and drive them out (Numbers 22:6, 11). The verb is the usual one for fighting, and it treats his plan as an act of war.

decisions.choice: sent and summoned: sent messengers to call him
decisions.reason: Balak sent elders of Moab and Midian to bring Balaam (Numbers 22:5-7).

decisions.choice: sent for; put a curse on / asked him to curse
decisions.reason: "Sent and summoned" is one action, so Balanced and Readable say "sent for".

source.text: וְלֹ֥א אָבִ֖יתִי לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ לְבִלְעָ֑ם וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ בָּרוֹךְ֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וָאַצִּ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And not I was willing to listen to Balaam, and he blessed indeed you, and I rescued you from his hand.

en.L: But I was not willing to listen to Balaam, and he indeed blessed you; and I rescued you from his hand.
en.B: But I would not listen to Balaam. Instead he blessed you over and over, and I rescued you from his power.
en.R: But I refused to listen to Balaam. So he blessed you time after time, and I saved you from his power.

sw.L: Lakini sikutaka kumsikiliza Balaamu, naye akawabariki kweli; nami nikawaokoa kutoka mkononi mwake.
sw.B: Lakini sikukubali kumsikiliza Balaamu. Badala yake aliwabariki tena na tena, nami nikawaokoa kutoka mkononi mwake.
sw.R: Lakini nilikataa kumsikiliza Balaamu. Kwa hiyo aliwabariki mara kwa mara, nami nikawaokoa kutoka mkononi mwake.

es.L: Pero no quise escuchar a Balaam, y él de cierto {{plural_you:los|os}} bendijo; y yo {{plural_you:los|os}} libré de su mano.
es.B: Pero yo no quise escuchar a Balaam. En cambio, él {{plural_you:los|os}} bendijo una y otra vez, y yo {{plural_you:los|os}} libré de su poder.
es.R: Pero yo no quise escuchar a Balaam. Así que él {{plural_you:los|os}} bendijo una y otra vez, y yo {{plural_you:los|os}} salvé de su poder.

decisions.choice: I was not willing to listen to Balaam: God turned the curse into a blessing
decisions.reason: Moses said the same thing: the LORD would not listen to Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing because he loved Israel (Deuteronomy 23:6). In Numbers 23-24 every attempt to curse became a blessing.

decisions.choice: he indeed blessed you: a repeated verb that makes it emphatic
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: Balaam did nothing but bless. He blessed Israel three times, though he was hired to curse (Numbers 24:10).

decisions.choice: his hand: most likely Balak's power, though it could be Balaam's
decisions.reason: "His" most naturally points back to Balak, the king who fought against Israel (verse 9). It could also mean Balaam, whose curse God did not allow to harm Israel. "Hand" means power.

decisions.choice: over and over / time after time; power
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the emphasis of the doubled verb with "over and over" and "time after time", and say "power" for "hand". They keep "his" as the Hebrew does.

source.text: וַתַּעַבְר֣וּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּן֮ וַתָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־יְרִיחוֹ֒ וַיִּלָּחֲמ֣וּ בָכֶ֣ם בַּעֲלֵֽי־יְ֠רִיחוֹ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֨י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֜י וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֗י וְהַֽחִתִּי֙ וְהַגִּרְגָּשִׁ֔י הַֽחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י וָאֶתֵּ֥ן אוֹתָ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho, and fought against you [the] lords of Jericho, the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Girgashite, the Hivite and the Jebusite; and I gave them into your hand.

en.L: And you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho, and the lords of Jericho fought against you, the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Girgashites, the Hivites and the Jebusites; and I gave them into your hand.
en.B: Then you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The leading citizens of Jericho fought against you, and so did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites and Jebusites, but I handed them over to you.
en.R: Then you crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought against you. So did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites and Jebusites. But I let you defeat them all.

sw.L: Nanyi mkavuka Yordani mkafika Yeriko, na wenyeji wakuu wa Yeriko wakapigana nanyi, Waamori na Waperizi na Wakanaani na Wahiti na Wagirgashi, Wahivi na Wayebusi; nami nikawatia mkononi mwenu.
sw.B: Kisha mlivuka Yordani mkafika Yeriko. Wakuu wa Yeriko walipigana nanyi, na vivyo hivyo Waamori, Waperizi, Wakanaani, Wahiti, Wagirgashi, Wahivi na Wayebusi, lakini niliwatia mikononi mwenu.
sw.R: Kisha mlivuka Mto Yordani mkafika Yeriko. Watu wa Yeriko walipigana nanyi. Vivyo hivyo Waamori, Waperizi, Wakanaani, Wahiti, Wagirgashi, Wahivi na Wayebusi. Lakini niliwawezesha kuwashinda wote.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:cruzaron|cruzasteis}} el Jordán y {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} a Jericó, y los señores de Jericó pelearon contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los amorreos, y los ferezeos, y los cananeos, y los hititas, y los gergeseos, los heveos y los jebuseos; y los entregué en {{plural_you:su mano|vuestra mano}}.
es.B: Luego {{plural_you:cruzaron|cruzasteis}} el Jordán y {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} a Jericó. Los principales de Jericó pelearon contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y también los amorreos, ferezeos, cananeos, hititas, gergeseos, heveos y jebuseos, pero yo {{plural_you:se los|os los}} entregué.
es.R: Luego {{plural_you:cruzaron|cruzasteis}} el río Jordán y {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} a Jericó. La gente de Jericó peleó contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. También pelearon los amorreos, ferezeos, cananeos, hititas, gergeseos, heveos y jebuseos. Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} di la victoria sobre todos ellos.

decisions.choice: the lords of Jericho: its leading citizens, the landowners of the city
decisions.reason: The word means "owners" or "masters", and with a town's name it means its citizens, especially those with land and power (Judges 9:2). Jericho shut its gates against Israel (6:1), and that resistance is counted here as fighting.

decisions.choice: the Amorites ... the Jebusites: all the peoples of the land, who fought after Jericho
decisions.reason: The list comes straight after "the lords of Jericho" without "and". Jericho was not a city of seven peoples, so the list sums up all who fought Israel in the land in chapters 6-12. It is the usual list of the peoples of Canaan (3:10).

decisions.choice: the leading citizens / the people of Jericho; and so did
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense of "lords" and add "and so did" to join the list to the sentence, following meaning decision m2. The Hebrew uses each people's name in the singular as a group name, so the English names are plural.

source.text: וָאֶשְׁלַ֤ח לִפְנֵיכֶם֙ אֶת־הַצִּרְעָ֔ה וַתְּגָ֤רֶשׁ אוֹתָם֙ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֔ם שְׁנֵ֖י מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֑י לֹ֥א בְחַרְבְּךָ֖ וְלֹ֥א בְקַשְׁתֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I sent before you the hornet, and it drove out them from before you, two kings of the Amorites; not by your sword and not by your bow.

en.L: And I sent the hornet before you, and it drove them out from before you, the two kings of the Amorites; not by your sword and not by your bow.
en.B: I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove them out before you, the two Amorite kings. It was not your sword or your bow that did it.
en.R: I sent hornets ahead of you. They chased away the two kings of the Amorites. You did not win with your own swords and bows.

sw.L: Nami nikatuma mavu mbele yenu, nayo yakawafukuza mbele yenu, wale wafalme wawili wa Waamori; si kwa upanga wako wala si kwa upinde wako.
sw.B: Nilituma mavu mbele yenu, nayo yakawafukuza mbele yenu, wale wafalme wawili wa Waamori. Haikuwa kwa upanga wako wala kwa upinde wako.
sw.R: Nilituma mavu mbele yenu. Yaliwafukuza wale wafalme wawili wa Waamori. Hamkushinda kwa panga na pinde zenu wenyewe.

es.L: Y envié delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} el avispón, y los expulsó de delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los dos reyes de los amorreos; no con {{plural_you:su espada|vuestra espada}} ni con {{plural_you:su arco|vuestro arco}}.
es.B: Envié el avispón delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y los expulsó delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, a los dos reyes amorreos. No fue {{plural_you:su espada|vuestra espada}} ni {{plural_you:su arco|vuestro arco}} lo que lo hizo.
es.R: Envié avispones delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Ellos ahuyentaron a los dos reyes de los amorreos. No {{plural_you:ganaron|ganasteis}} con {{plural_you:sus propias espadas|vuestras propias espadas}} y arcos.

decisions.choice: the hornet: the meaning of the word is uncertain
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 23:28 and Deuteronomy 7:20, the only other places the word appears. It is usually taken as "hornet", a stinging insect, whether real or a picture of a terror that drives people to flight. Some take it as "panic" or "plague". Either way God himself drove the enemy out.

decisions.choice: two kings of the Amorites, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The two Amorite kings are Sihon and Og, east of the Jordan (verse 8; 2:10; 9:10). The ancient Greek translation reads "twelve kings of the Amorites", which would refer to kings west of the Jordan. The Hebrew reading is kept.

decisions.choice: not by your sword and not by your bow: the victory was God's
decisions.reason: "Your" is singular here, speaking to Israel as one. The land was not won by Israel's weapons but by God (Psalm 44:4, 7).

decisions.choice: It was not your sword or your bow that did it / You did not win with your own swords and bows
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the short closing phrase into a full sentence. Readable uses "hornets" in the plural, as in Exodus 23:28, since the singular names the kind of creature.

decisions.choice: "el avispón" (L, B); "avispones" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names a stinging insect, the hornet, as in Exodus 23:28 and Deuteronomy 7:20; Spanish has the exact word. Readable makes it plural, as the English Readable does, since the Hebrew singular stands for the whole swarm.

source.text: וָאֶתֵּ֨ן לָכֶ֜ם אֶ֣רֶץ׀אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יָגַ֣עְתָּ בָּ֗הּ וְעָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־בְנִיתֶ֔ם וַתֵּשְׁב֖וּ בָּהֶ֑ם כְּרָמִ֤ים וְזֵיתִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־נְטַעְתֶּ֔ם אַתֶּ֖ם אֹכְלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I gave to you a land on which not you had labored, and cities which not you had built, and you live in them; vineyards and olive groves which not you planted, you [are] eating.

en.L: And I gave you a land on which you had not labored, and cities that you had not built, and you live in them; vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant, you are eating [from them].'
en.B: I gave you a land you had not worked for and towns you had not built, and you live in them. You eat from vineyards and olive groves you did not plant.'
en.R: I gave you land that you did not work for, and towns that you did not build. Now you live in those towns. You eat grapes and olives from vines and trees you did not plant.'

sw.L: Nami nikawapa nchi ambayo hamkuitaabikia, na miji ambayo hamkuijenga, nanyi mnakaa ndani yake; mashamba ya mizabibu na mizeituni ambayo hamkuipanda, mnakula [matunda yake].'
sw.B: Niliwapa nchi ambayo hamkuifanyia kazi na miji ambayo hamkuijenga, nanyi mnaishi ndani yake. Mnakula matunda ya mashamba ya mizabibu na mizeituni ambayo hamkuipanda.'

es.L: Y {{plural_you:les|os}} di una tierra en la que no {{plural_you:habían|habíais}} trabajado, y ciudades que no {{plural_you:habían|habíais}} edificado, y {{plural_you:habitan|habitáis}} en ellas; viñas y olivares que no {{plural_you:plantaron|plantasteis}}, [de ellos] {{plural_you:comen|coméis}}”.

decisions.choice: and now: Joshua turns from God's story to the call it leads to
decisions.reason: "And now" draws the conclusion from verses 2-13. Joshua speaks here in his own voice again: because of all God has done, Israel must choose to serve him.

decisions.choice: fear the LORD: hold him in awe and reverence that shows in obedience
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is not to be terrified of him but to honor him as God, and so to keep his ways (Deuteronomy 6:13; 10:12).

decisions.choice: in wholeness and in faithfulness: with an undivided heart and with loyalty
decisions.reason: The first word means whole, complete, without blemish, here a service with nothing held back. The second means what is firm and reliable: faithfulness, loyalty, truth. Together they mean serving God sincerely and staying true to him.

decisions.choice: remove the gods: the same command Jacob gave at Shechem
decisions.reason: At Shechem Jacob told his household to put away the foreign gods among them, and buried them under the oak there (Genesis 35:2-4). The people's ancestors served other gods beyond the River (verse 2), and some Israelites had served the gods of Egypt (Ezekiel 20:7-8).

decisions.choice: with a whole heart and with faithfulness / with all your heart, and be faithful; have deep respect for (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "wholeness" means in serving God. Readable says "have deep respect for" for "fear", as Deuteronomy does, so young readers do not think of being frightened.

decisions.choice: "teman" (L, B), "respeten profundamente" (R); "con integridad y con fidelidad" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "fear", the awe and reverence owed to the LORD; Readable says "respeten profundamente", as the English Readable says "have deep respect". The pronoun joined to the verb ("sírvanle") takes no deity pronoun span, as set at 22:5; the free "a él" in Readable does.

decisions.choice: evil in your eyes: seems wrong or displeasing to you
decisions.reason: "Good" or "evil in someone's eyes" means what a person thinks right or wrong, pleasing or not (Genesis 28:8; Numbers 22:34).

decisions.choice: choose: the choice Joshua offers is between other gods, not between the LORD and others
decisions.reason: Joshua does not set the LORD out as one option among many. If Israel will not serve the LORD, it must still serve someone, and the only other choices are the old gods of Mesopotamia or the gods of the Canaanites around them. The challenge is meant to bring the people to choose the LORD freely and on purpose.

decisions.choice: from beyond the River, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "in beyond the River"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "from beyond the River". Both describe the same gods, those served in the land beyond the Euphrates.

decisions.choice: I and my house: Joshua and his household, everyone under his care
decisions.reason: "House" here means a household, the family and all who live under its head (Genesis 18:19). The pronoun "I" comes first for emphasis: whatever others choose, Joshua has already chosen.

decisions.choice: whom will you serve ...?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "whom you will serve, whether ... or ..." is an indirect question. All three levels turn it into a direct question, which keeps the two choices side by side and reads clearly aloud.

decisions.choice: My household and I / My family and I
decisions.reason: Balanced says "household", the closest English word for this sense of "house". Readable says "family". Both put "I" second, as English normally does; Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

decisions.choice: "Pero en cuanto a mí y a mi casa, nosotros serviremos" (L); "Mi familia y yo serviremos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which sets Joshua and his household first and then says "we will serve". Balanced and Readable say it the natural Spanish way, naming the others before oneself, and "familia" for the household, as the English says "household" and "family".

decisions.choice: a profane thing for us: an exclamation rejecting something as unthinkable
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to make common, profane". Said with "to us", it means "that would be an outrage for us", a strong refusal (Genesis 18:25; 44:7, 17).

decisions.choice: forsake: leave, abandon someone one belongs to
decisions.reason: The verb is used for abandoning a person or a covenant (Deuteronomy 29:24; 31:16). Joshua takes it up in verse 20.

decisions.choice: We would never / We will never
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the force of the exclamation in plain words. The people's answer runs on to the end of verse 18.

decisions.choice: "¡Lejos esté de nosotros" (L); "¡Nunca ...!" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls the thought a profane thing, something unthinkable; Spanish says that with the fixed phrase "lejos esté de nosotros", as at 22:29. Balanced and Readable say it plainly, as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: For Yahweh our God, he [is] the one bringing up us and our fathers from [the] land of Egypt, from [the] house of slaves, and who did before our eyes the signs the great the these, and kept us in all the way which we went in it, and among all the peoples which we passed through their midst.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the one who brought us and our fathers up from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves, and who did these great signs before our eyes, and kept us in all the way that we went and among all the peoples through whose midst we passed.
en.B: It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God who brought us and our ancestors up from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery. He did these great signs before our eyes, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept us safe all along the road we traveled and among all the peoples we passed through.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God brought us and our ancestors out of Egypt, where we were slaves. We saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do those great signs. He protected us everywhere we went, as we traveled through the lands of other nations.

es.L: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [es] quien nos sacó a nosotros y a nuestros padres de la tierra de Egipto, de la casa de esclavos, y quien hizo delante de nuestros ojos estas grandes señales, y nos guardó en todo el camino por el que anduvimos y entre todos los pueblos por en medio de los cuales pasamos.
es.B: Es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios quien nos sacó a nosotros y a nuestros antepasados de la tierra de Egipto, de la casa de esclavitud. Él hizo estas grandes señales ante nuestros ojos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos protegió en todo el camino que recorrimos y entre todos los pueblos por los que pasamos.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios nos sacó a nosotros y a nuestros antepasados de Egipto, donde éramos esclavos. Nosotros {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vimos hacer esas grandes señales. Él nos protegió en todas partes, mientras viajábamos por las tierras de otras naciones.

decisions.choice: the house of slaves: Egypt, where Israel lived as slaves
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from the opening of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2; Deuteronomy 5:6). The people answer Joshua with the words of the covenant itself.

decisions.choice: he is the one who brought us up: the LORD and no other
decisions.reason: The pronoun "he" is stressed: the LORD himself, not any of the gods of verse 15, brought Israel out. The people count themselves with their ancestors among those he rescued, as God's words did in verses 5-7.

decisions.choice: signs: acts of power that show who God is
decisions.reason: The plagues and wonders in Egypt were signs, done so that Israel and Egypt would know the LORD (Exodus 10:1-2; Deuteronomy 6:22).

decisions.choice: kept us: guarded and protected us
decisions.reason: The verb means to watch over and guard, as God promised to guard Israel on the way (Exodus 23:20).

decisions.choice: house of slaves / house of slavery / where we were slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" stays at every level here, because the point is Israel's slavery in Egypt, as the style guide sets out for Exodus 20:2.

decisions.choice: "nyumba ya watumwa" (Literal), "nyumba ya utumwa" (Balanced), "tulipokuwa watumwa" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Israel's slavery in Egypt is one of the places where the Hebrew word for slave keeps its full force at every level, as the Pentateuch note says, so Swahili uses "mtumwa" and "utumwa" here, not "mtumishi".

sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwafukuza mbele yetu watu wote, hata Waamori walioishi katika nchi. Kwa hiyo sisi nasi tutamtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye Mungu wetu."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwafukuza mbele yetu watu wote, hata Waamori walioishi katika nchi hii. Kwa hiyo sisi nasi tutamtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye Mungu wetu."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} expulsó de delante de nosotros a todos los pueblos, y a los amorreos que habitaban la tierra. También nosotros serviremos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [es] nuestro Dios».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} expulsó delante de nosotros a todos los pueblos, también a los amorreos que vivían en la tierra. Así que nosotros también serviremos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es nuestro Dios».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} echó delante de nosotros a todos los pueblos, aun a los amorreos que vivían en esta tierra. Así que nosotros también serviremos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es nuestro Dios».

decisions.choice: and the Amorites: the chief people of the land, named out of all the peoples
decisions.reason: The "and" picks out the Amorites from "all the peoples", as the people best known for living in the land (verses 8, 15). It means "and in particular" rather than a separate group.

decisions.choice: we too will serve: the people take up Joshua's own words
decisions.reason: "We too" answers Joshua's "I and my house, we will serve the LORD" (verse 15). The people join him in his choice, and the reason they give is what God has done for them.

decisions.choice: including / even
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the sense of the "and" (meaning decision m1). The people's answer, opened in verse 16, closes here.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶל־הָעָ֗ם לֹ֤א תֽוּכְלוּ֙ לַעֲבֹ֣ד אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים קְדֹשִׁ֖ים ה֑וּא אֵֽל־קַנּ֣וֹא ה֔וּא לֹֽא־יִשָּׂ֥א לְפִשְׁעֲכֶ֖ם וּלְחַטֹּאותֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joshua to the people, not you will be able to serve Yahweh, for [a] God holy he [is]; [a] God jealous he [is]; not he will forgive your transgression and your sins.

en.L: And Joshua said to the people, "You will not be able to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for a holy God [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; a jealous God [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not forgive your transgression and your sins.
en.B: Joshua said to the people, "You will not be able to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a holy God, a jealous God; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not pardon your rebellion and your sins.
en.R: Joshua told the people, "You are not able to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He is a holy God. He is a jealous God, who wants you to belong only to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He will not forgive you when you rebel against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and sin.

sw.L: Na Yoshua akawaambia watu, "Hamtaweza kumtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana Mungu mtakatifu [ni] {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}; Mungu mwenye wivu [ni] {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hatasamehe makosa yenu na dhambi zenu.
sw.B: Yoshua akawaambia watu, "Hamtaweza kumtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni Mungu mtakatifu, Mungu mwenye wivu; hatausamehe uasi wenu na dhambi zenu.
sw.R: Yoshua akawaambia watu, "Hamwezi kumtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Yeye ni Mungu mtakatifu. Ni Mungu mwenye wivu, anayetaka muwe {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} peke yake. Hatawasamehe mkimwasi na kutenda dhambi.

es.L: Y dijo Josué al pueblo: «No {{plural_you:podrán|podréis}} servir {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque Dios santo [es] {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; Dios celoso [es] {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; no perdonará {{plural_you:sus transgresiones|vuestras transgresiones}} ni {{plural_you:sus pecados|vuestros pecados}}.
es.B: Josué dijo al pueblo: «No {{plural_you:podrán|podréis}} servir {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es un Dios santo, un Dios celoso; no {{plural_you:les|os}} perdonará {{plural_you:su rebelión|vuestra rebelión}} ni {{plural_you:sus pecados|vuestros pecados}}.
es.R: Josué le dijo al pueblo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes no pueden|Vosotros no podéis}} servir {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Él es un Dios santo. Es un Dios celoso, que quiere que {{plural_you:ustedes sean|vosotros seáis}} solo de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. No {{plural_you:les|os}} perdonará cuando {{plural_you:se rebelen|os rebeléis}} contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{plural_you:pequen|pequéis}}.

decisions.choice: you will not be able to serve the LORD: a warning that their promise is too easy
decisions.reason: Joshua is not refusing the people or telling them not to try. He warns that serving this God is not something they can take on lightly, as if he were one god among many. Their later history bears out the warning (Judges 2:11-13).

decisions.choice: a holy God: the adjective is plural, agreeing with the plural form of the word for God
decisions.reason: The word for God has a plural form, and here the adjective "holy" agrees with it, as "living" does in 1 Samuel 17:26. It still speaks of one God. Holy means set apart, wholly other and pure, so that sin cannot stand before him (Leviticus 19:2).

decisions.choice: a jealous God: a God who demands his people's loyalty for himself alone
decisions.reason: This is not petty envy but the claim of a husband on his wife's faithfulness, which will not share her with rivals. It is the reason given in the commandment against other gods (Exodus 20:5; 34:14).

decisions.choice: will not forgive your transgression and your sins: he will not let deliberate unfaithfulness pass
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift up and carry away. "Transgression" is rebellion, a breaking of faith with one's lord; "sins" are wrongs in general. Joshua does not deny that God forgives (Exodus 34:6-7); he warns that turning to other gods is a rebellion God will not treat lightly (verse 20; Exodus 23:21).

decisions.choice: rebellion (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "transgression". Balanced and Readable say "rebellion", which is the sense of the word.

decisions.choice: who wants you to belong only to him
decisions.reason: Readable explains "jealous", following meaning decision m3, because the English word usually suggests envy.

decisions.choice: "un Dios celoso"
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:5: the LORD's jealousy is his claim to his people's whole loyalty, not envy. Readable explains it in words, as the English Readable does.

en.L: If you forsake {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve foreign gods, then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will turn and do you harm and make an end of you, after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done you good."
en.B: If you leave {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve the gods of foreigners, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will turn against you. He will bring harm on you and put an end to you, after all the good {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done you."
en.R: If you leave {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve the gods of other nations, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will turn against you. He has been good to you, but then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring trouble on you and destroy you."

sw.L: Mkimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kutumikia miungu ya kigeni, ndipo atageuka na kuwatenda mabaya na kuwakomesha, baada ya kuwa amewatendea mema."
sw.B: Mkimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kutumikia miungu ya wageni, atawageukia. Atawaletea mabaya na kuwakomesha, baada ya mema yote aliyowatendea."
sw.R: Mkimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kutumikia miungu ya mataifa mengine, atawageukia. Amekuwa mwema kwenu, lakini ndipo atawaletea taabu na kuwaangamiza."

es.L: Si {{plural_you:abandonan|abandonáis}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:sirven|servís}} a dioses extranjeros, entonces {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se volverá y {{plural_you:les|os}} hará mal y acabará con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, después de que {{plural_you:les|os}} haya hecho bien».
es.B: Si {{plural_you:dejan|dejáis}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:sirven|servís}} a los dioses de los extranjeros, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se volverá contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} traerá desgracia y acabará con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, después de todo el bien que {{plural_you:les|os}} ha hecho».
es.R: Si {{plural_you:dejan|dejáis}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:sirven|servís}} a los dioses de otras naciones, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se volverá contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Él ha sido bueno con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero entonces {{plural_you:les|os}} traerá desgracias y {{plural_you:los|os}} destruirá».

decisions.choice: gods of foreignness: the gods of foreign peoples
decisions.reason: The phrase means gods that belong to other nations, strangers to Israel (Genesis 35:2; Deuteronomy 31:16).

decisions.choice: he will turn: he will change from doing good to doing harm
decisions.reason: "Turn" here means turn around: the God who did them good will become their enemy. Moses gave the same warning (Deuteronomy 8:19-20; 28:63).

decisions.choice: after he has done you good: his past kindness will not shield them
decisions.reason: The phrase does not mean that the harm will come later in time only. It means that God's good gifts so far, told in verses 2-13, will not protect a people who forsake him.

decisions.choice: will turn against you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "turn against", the sense of meaning decision m2, because "turn" alone is unclear in English.

en.L: And the people said to Joshua, "No, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} we will serve!"
en.B: But the people said to Joshua, "No! We will serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: But the people answered Joshua, "No! We will serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

sw.B: Lakini watu wakamwambia Yoshua, "Hapana! Tutamtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Lakini watu wakamjibu Yoshua, "Hapana! Tutamtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

es.B: Pero el pueblo le dijo a Josué: «¡No! Serviremos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}».
es.R: Pero el pueblo le respondió a Josué: «¡No! Serviremos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}».

decisions.choice: No, but the LORD we will serve: they reject Joshua's warning and repeat their promise
decisions.reason: "No" answers Joshua's "you will not be able" (verse 19). The name of the LORD is put first for emphasis: him and no other.

decisions.choice: No! We will serve the LORD.
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out "but" and use the usual English order. Literal keeps the Hebrew order to show the emphasis.
